title: Polynomial-local regular-sequence presentation at an LCI prime
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There exist $h\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, integers $m,c\geq0$, $Q=k[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in Q$, and a $k$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:Q/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_h$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], where $S_h$ is a global complete intersection with this presentation. Write $\mathfrak q_h=\mathfrak qS_h$ and let $\mathfrak b\subset Q$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q_h$ under $Q\to Q/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\theta}S_h$. Then $Q_{\mathfrak b}$ is a regular local $k$-algebra [def-weil-regular-scheme] essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], the sequence $f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1$ is regular and lies in its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and the canonical map $Q_{\mathfrak b}/(f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a $k$-algebra isomorphism. This map is induced by $r/t\mapsto\theta(\bar r)/\theta(\bar t)$ followed by $(S_h)_{\mathfrak q_h}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$, whose fraction formula is $(a/h^i)/(b/h^j)\mapsto ah^j/(h^ib)$. Empty sequences and zero-variable polynomial rings are allowed; if $S=0$ there is no prime to which the assertion applies.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], choose a principal-open cover $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_iD(g_i)$ with each $S_{g_i}$ a global complete intersection. The point $\mathfrak q$ belongs to some $D(g_i)$, so put $h=g_i\notin\mathfrak q$. Once $S_h\ne0$ is checked in step 2, the same definition supplies $m,c$, $Q=k[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and $\theta:Q/J\cong S_h$ with $\dim(Q/J)=\dim S_h=m-c$. An algebra isomorphism identifies prime chains in both directions, so the dimension equality passes to $Q/J$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](1) to $S\to S_h$ and $W=\{h^i:i\ge0\}$. Since $h\notin\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q$ is prime, $W\cap\mathfrak q=\varnothing$. Thus $\mathfrak q_h=\mathfrak qS_h$ is a proper prime and contracts to $\mathfrak q$; in particular $S_h\ne0$, completing the check in step 1. With its presentation chosen, let $\alpha:Q\to S_h$ be $\theta$ after the quotient map and put $\mathfrak b=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q_h)$. This is prime: $1$ is not in its inverse image and $\alpha(rs)=\alpha(r)\alpha(s)$ shows the prime-ideal implication. Moreover $J\subseteq\mathfrak b$ because $\alpha(f_i)=0$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $Q_{\mathfrak b}$ is a regular local ring. It is essentially of finite type over $k$: $Q$ is generated by its finitely many variables over $k$, and $Q_{\mathfrak b}$ is precisely its localization at $Q\setminus\mathfrak b$, which is the condition in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. The finite-generation assertion follows by writing each polynomial as a finite sum of monomials in those variables [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] hold for $Q,J,Q/J,\mathfrak b$: the quotient is nonzero by $\theta$ and step 2, has dimension $m-c$ by step 1, and $J\subseteq\mathfrak b$ by step 2. Hence $f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in $Q_{\mathfrak b}$. Each term lies in $\mathfrak bQ_{\mathfrak b}$ because $f_i\in J\subseteq\mathfrak b$, and this is the maximal ideal by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Let $\bar{\mathfrak b}=\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak q_h)\subset Q/J$. The quotient-localization isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] sends $[r/t]$ to $\bar r/\bar t$. Applying $\theta$ to numerator and denominator gives an isomorphism to $(S_h)_{\mathfrak q_h}$, with inverse obtained using $\theta^{-1}$. The fraction equivalence relation is preserved because these ring maps preserve products and zero. The localized ideal $JQ_{\mathfrak b}$ equals $(f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1)$: localize an expression $\sum a_if_i$, and conversely each $f_i/1$ is in the extended ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso](2), $(S_h)_{\mathfrak q_h}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$. Its inverse to $a/s\mapsto(a/1)/(s/1)$ is $(a/h^i)/(b/h^j)\mapsto ah^j/(h^ib)$: $b/h^j\notin\mathfrak q_h$ means $b\notin\mathfrak q$, so the denominator is permitted. Substitution in each composite cancels the powers of the unit $h$. All maps fix $k$, giving exactly the asserted $k$-algebra isomorphism. The argument allows $c=0$ and $m=0$; $S=0$ has no proper prime.

lean.statement: theorem exists_prime_polynomial_local_presentation (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (hlci : IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S) (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] : ∃ (h : S), h ∉ q ∧ ∃ (m c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (θ : (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ≃ₐ[k] Localization.Away h), c ≤ m ∧ topologicalKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away h)) = (↑(m - c) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∃ (b : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)), b.asIdeal = (q.map (algebraMap S (Localization.Away h))).comap (θ.toRingHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal) ∧ Algebra.EssFiniteType k (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal) ((List.ofFn f).map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin c, algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal) (f i) ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal)) ∧ ∃ (ι : Localization.Away h →ₐ[k] Localization.AtPrime q) (e : (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin c ↦ algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal) (f i)))) ≃ₐ[k] Localization.AtPrime q), (∀ s : S, ι (algebraMap S (Localization.Away h) s) = algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime q) s) ∧ ∀ r : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (Localization.AtPrime b.asIdeal) r)) = ι (θ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) r))
